title: Property of the descended quasi-compact open
statement:
The constructed $W_{\lambda_W}$ is quasi-compact, and its inverse image in
$Y$ is exactly $W$.

proof.text: Unfold def-nagata-qc-open-descent. Name the finite set F, its selected upper bound w, the object j above the base stage, and each transition t_a from j to the lift stage. The inequalities defining these transitions are precisely le_directedFiniteUpperBound (lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound). Write V_a for the inverse-image affine chart at j and g_ak for the transported lift. The constructed open is the finite supremum of the basic opens D(g_ak). Each V_a is affine by base change of the affine transition (Stacks 01SD); hence each D(g_ak) is affine and compact, and their finite union is compact.

For each a,k, Scheme.basicOpen_appLE expresses D(g_ak) as V_a intersected with the transition preimage of D(lift_ak). Pull this equality back along the limit projection. The cone identity identifies projection followed by transition with the lift-stage projection, and baseChangeCone_π_app_fst identifies the inverse image of V_a with the original limit chart. Apply Scheme.basicOpen_appLE in reverse for that chart and rewrite by the supplied hlift equation. This proves that each D(g_ak) pulls back to D(f_ak). These basic-open identities are the restricted-open form of lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-pullback.

Inverse image commutes with the two finite suprema. Use the previous basic-open identities and the given hpresentation equations to obtain the supremum over a of W intersected with the inverse image of U_a. Distribute intersection over supremum, use that inverse image preserves supremum, and rewrite with hcover. The result is W intersected with top, hence W. This also handles m=0 and r_a=0 without additional nonemptiness assumptions.

blueprint_update.statement:
The constructed $W_{\lambda_W}$ is quasi-compact, and its inverse image in
$Y$ is exactly $W$.

proof.text:
A finite union of basic opens is quasi-compact. Every lifted defining
function has reached the common stage $\lambda_W$, and base change sends
$D(f_{ak,\lambda_W})$ to $D(f_{ak})$. Taking the finite union therefore
recovers precisely the selected basic-open presentation of $W$.
